title: Ingress

header.html: Use Ingress rules to expose applications
Kubernetes v1.37.0 (3-node test cluster, containerd 2.3.4, Traefik as the Ingress controller)

toc.title: What Ingress adds to a Service

html:
1What Ingress adds to a Service

A Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer exposes one application per port or per address. An Ingress exposes many HTTP and HTTPS applications behind one entry point, and chooses the backend by the host name and the path of the request.

Two parts work together:

Part What it is
Ingress (the object) the rules: "host a.example.com goes to Service a"
Ingress controller (a program running in the cluster) reads the Ingress objects and does the routing (Traefik, NGINX-based controllers, HAProxy, cloud controllers)

An Ingress does nothing without a controller. A controller serves only Ingresses that belong to its IngressClass: spec.ingressClassName names the class. The CKAD environment already has a controller; read k get ingressclass to see the class name to use. (This course's labs use Traefik with the class traefik. The exam controller can differ: the objects are the same, only the class name changes.)

2An Ingress object

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: routes
  namespace: ing1
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
  - host: a.example.com                 # optional; omit it to match any host
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: a                     # a Service in the SAME namespace
            port: {number: 80}          # or {name: http}
  - host: b.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - {path: /, pathType: Prefix, backend: {service: {name: b, port: {number: 80}}}}
Field Meaning
host the Host header of the request; without it the rule matches every host
path the URL path
pathType required: Prefix (/api matches /api and /api/x), Exact (only that path), ImplementationSpecific (the controller decides)
backend.service the Service name and port that receives the traffic
defaultBackend where requests go that match no rule
tls hosts and the Secret that holds the certificate (below)

The backend Service is in the same namespace as the Ingress. The Ingress is only the rule: the Service must exist and have endpoints.

Default backend. defaultBackend receives the requests that match no rule. Controllers differ in how they honor it next to host rules: on the Traefik test cluster it works reliably when it is the only setting of an Ingress of its own (a second Ingress holds the host rules), so test it with a request to an unknown host.

Path matching. When several paths match, the longest wins: with /api and / both present, /api/users goes to the /api backend. A path rule does not rewrite the URL: the backend still receives /api/users, so the app must serve that path (rewrites need a controller-specific annotation or middleware).

3Create one fast

k create ingress routes --class=traefik \
   --rule="a.example.com/*=a:80" --rule="b.example.com/*=b:80"      # host rules; /* means Prefix
k create ingress paths --class=traefik \
   --rule="app.example.com/api*=api:80" --rule="app.example.com/*=web:80"
k create ingress secure --class=traefik --rule="secure.example.com/*=a:80,tls=web-tls"
k create ingress fallback --class=traefik --default-backend=a:80
k get ingress -A
k describe ingress routes                     # Rules table and the Backend with its endpoints

In --rule, a path ending in * becomes Prefix; without * it is Exact. For a default backend plus rules, generate YAML (--dry-run=client -o yaml) and add defaultBackend.

4TLS

HTTPS needs a certificate. Put the certificate and key in a TLS Secret, in the same namespace as the Ingress, and name it in tls:

k create secret tls web-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key -n ing2

spec:
  tls:
  - hosts: [secure.example.com]
    secretName: web-tls
  rules: [...]

The Secret must be of type kubernetes.io/tls with the keys tls.crt and tls.key (a generic Secret with the same files is not accepted by controllers). The certificate's name should match the host.

5Test and troubleshoot

Test from inside the cluster, with a Host header and without DNS: k run t --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- --header "Host: a.example.com" http://<controller-service>. From a machine that can reach the controller: curl -H "Host: a.example.com" http://<ip>/.

Symptom Likely cause Check
404 from the controller for every request no Ingress accepted for that host: wrong ingressClassName (a class that no controller serves) or wrong host k get ingressclass, k get ingress -o yaml
404 only for some paths path or pathType does not match k describe ingress
502 or 503 from the controller the backend Service has no endpoints, or the name or port is wrong k describe ingress (Backend line), k get endpoints
service "x" not found in the describe output the backend Service name has a typo k get svc
Works with HTTP, certificate error with HTTPS wrong Secret type, wrong namespace or a certificate for another host k get secret -o yaml
Exam tip

. Read the IngressClass first: k get ingressclass. A task that gives you "the Ingress controller is installed" still expects ingressClassName to be set on your Ingress.

Exam tip

. k describe ingress <name> lists the backend with its resolved endpoints; <error: endpoints "x" not found> means the Service name or the Service itself is wrong.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m15 -->

Lab 15.1: ingress host routing

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m15-01-ingress-host-routing)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

An Ingress controller (IngressClass traefik) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing1, the Services a and b (port 80) exist. Create an Ingress named routes that uses the class traefik and sends requests for the host a.example.com to the Service a and requests for the host b.example.com to the Service b, for all paths.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n ing1 create ingress routes --class=traefik --rule="a.example.com/*=a:80" --rule="b.example.com/*=b:80"
kubectl -n ing1 get ingress routes
sleep 5

Lab 15.2: ingress path routing

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m15-02-ingress-path-routing)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

An Ingress controller (IngressClass traefik) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing5, the Services web and api (port 80) exist. Create an Ingress named paths that uses the class traefik and serves the host app.example.com: requests for the path /api (prefix) go to the Service api, and all other requests (the path /, prefix) go to the Service web.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n ing5 create ingress paths --class=traefik --rule="app.example.com/api*=api:80" --rule="app.example.com/*=web:80"
kubectl -n ing5 get ingress paths
sleep 6

Lab 15.3: ingress tls

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m15-03-ingress-tls)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace ing2, the Service a exists. A certificate and key for secure.example.com are in ~/answers/tls.crt and ~/answers/tls.key. Create a TLS Secret named web-tls from them, and an Ingress named secure (class traefik) that serves the host secure.example.com from the Service a on port 80 and uses the Secret for HTTPS.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n ing2 create secret tls web-tls --cert=$HOME/answers/tls.crt --key=$HOME/answers/tls.key
kubectl -n ing2 create ingress secure --class=traefik --rule="secure.example.com/*=a:80,tls=web-tls"
kubectl -n ing2 get ingress secure
sleep 5

Lab 15.4: fix ingress class

Domain: Networking | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m15-04-fix-ingress-class)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace ing3, the Ingress site for the host site.example.com (backend Service a) is not served: the controller answers 404. Find the cause and fix the Ingress (keep its name and rules) so that site.example.com returns the page of Service a.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n ing3 get ingress site -o jsonpath='{.spec.ingressClassName}'; echo
kubectl -n ing3 patch ingress site --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"ingressClassName":"traefik"}}'
sleep 6

Lab 15.5: fix ingress backend

Domain: Networking | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m15-05-fix-ingress-backend)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace ing4, requests for shop.example.com through the Ingress shop fail. The Service web is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Ingress so that shop.example.com returns the page of the Service web.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n ing4 describe ingress shop | grep -i -A2 backend
kubectl -n ing4 get svc
kubectl -n ing4 patch ingress shop --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/rules/0/http/paths/0/backend/service/name","value":"web"}]'
sleep 6

Lab 15.6: ingress default backend

Domain: Networking | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m15-06-ingress-default-backend)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace ing6, the Services a and b (port 80) exist. Create an Ingress named b-route (class traefik) that sends requests for the host b.example.com to the Service b, and a second Ingress named fallback (class traefik) that has only a default backend (defaultBackend) pointing to the Service a, so that all other requests are answered by a.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n ing6 create ingress b-route --class=traefik --rule="b.example.com/*=b:80"
kubectl -n ing6 create ingress fallback --class=traefik --default-backend=a:80
kubectl -n ing6 get ingress
sleep 6

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What is the difference between an Ingress and an Ingress controller?

Show the answer

The Ingress is the routing rule object; the controller is the program that reads it and routes the traffic.

R2Which field links an Ingress to a controller?

Show the answer

spec.ingressClassName.

R3What does pathType: Prefix with /api match?

Show the answer

/api and every path below it, such as /api/users.

R4In which namespace must the backend Service be?

Show the answer

The same namespace as the Ingress.

R5Which Secret type does Ingress TLS need?

Show the answer

kubernetes.io/tls with tls.crt and tls.key, in the Ingress's namespace.

R6What does defaultBackend do?

Show the answer

It receives the requests that match no rule.

R7What do you check first when every request returns 404?

Show the answer

The IngressClass name and the host in the Ingress.

R8Does a path rule rewrite the URL?

Show the answer

No; the backend receives the original path.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Parts Ingress object (rules) + controller (does the work); ingressClassName
Rules host, path, pathType (Prefix, Exact), backend.service name + port
Create k create ingress NAME --class=C --rule="host/path*=svc:port"
Default defaultBackend for unmatched requests
TLS k create secret tls; spec.tls[].secretName; same namespace
Longest path wins /api beats /
Debug get ingressclass, describe ingress, get endpoints, Host header test
